title: Extraction and visualization of orientation data from virtual geologic surfaces with MATLAB®
author: Welker, Hogan, et al.

steps.title: Prepare high‑resolution triangular mesh
steps.instruction: Obtain a point‑cloud representation of the geological surface (e.g., LiDAR, photogrammetry, seismic) and discretize it into a high‑resolution triangular surface using a geologic modeling package such as Petrel®, GOCAD®, or a finite‑element pre‑processor like HyperMesh®; ensure the mesh resolution is sufficient to accurately represent the geometry (low‑resolution meshes may introduce significant errors).

substeps.instruction: Acquire or generate the point‑cloud data for the target surface.
Import the point cloud into the chosen modeling software.
Create a triangulated surface (mesh) from the point cloud, selecting a resolution that captures surface detail.

steps.title: Export triangle coordinates
steps.instruction: Export the Cartesian coordinates (X, Y, Z) of each triangle’s three vertices from the modeling software to a comma‑separated values file (*.csv) or a Microsoft Excel spreadsheet (*.xlsx).

substeps.instruction: Select the option to export mesh vertex data as a table of X, Y, Z coordinates for each triangle (three rows per triangle).
Save the table as a .csv file or an Excel workbook.

steps.title: Run MATLAB orientation script
steps.instruction: Open MATLAB, navigate to the folder containing the provided orientation‑extraction script, and execute it; when prompted, enter the name of the coordinate file you exported.

substeps.instruction: Start MATLAB and add the script’s directory to the path (e.g., `addpath('path/to/script')`).
Run the script (e.g., type the script name at the command prompt).
When MATLAB displays the prompt `filename`, type the exact name of the .csv or Excel file and press Enter.

steps.title: Generate attitude data files
steps.instruction: The script reads the triangular coordinates, computes normal vectors, strike, dip, and right‑hand‑rule dip‑direction using the three‑point vector method, and writes two output files: an ASCII text file (*.txt) and a new spreadsheet containing the calculated strike, dip, and dip‑direction values.

substeps.instruction: The script forms vectors `vector1` (XYZ2 → XYZ1) and `vector2` (XYZ2 → XYZ3).
It calculates the cross‑product `normalV` = `vector2` × `vector1` to obtain the triangle pole.
From `normalV` it derives strike, dip, and dip‑direction (right‑hand rule).
Results are saved as `CombinedResults` (strike, dip, dip‑direction) in a .txt file and as a spreadsheet.

steps.title: Create synthetic plots (optional)
steps.instruction: Use the generated attitude data with the same MATLAB script or with external software (e.g., Stereonet 10, Move™) to produce synthetic stereograms, polar tangent diagrams, or other graphical representations.

substeps.instruction: Import the output spreadsheet into the desired plotting program.
Generate the desired plot (e.g., polar tangent diagram) using the program’s functions.

steps.title: Adapt script for custom formats (optional)
steps.instruction: If your input or desired output format differs from the defaults, edit the script variables (e.g., `prompt`, `data`, `numRows`, `TangentPlotMatrix`) to match your file structure before re‑running the script.
